intro: Set unique items ka unordered collection hai. Iska asli kamaal membership test aur set algebra hai: union, intersection, difference — teenon O(len) me. Duplicate hatane aur "kaun se items dono me hain" wale sawaalon ka ye sabse seedha jawab hai.
theory: Set duplicate values store nahi karta; same value dobara add karne se size nahi badhta.
Set unordered hai, isliye indexing nahi hoti aur print order par bharosa nahi karna chahiye. Deterministic output ke liye sorted() use karo.
Membership test average O(1) hai (hash table), jabki list me O(n). Bade collections me `in` checks ke liye set better hai.
Set operations: `|` union, `&` intersection, `-` difference, `^` symmetric difference. In-place versions `|=`, `&=`, `-=`, `^=` available hain.
Set ke items hashable hone chahiye — list nahi, tuple haan. frozenset immutable aur hashable hota hai, isliye wo dict key ban sakta hai.
syntax:
tags = {'python', 'sql', 'ml'}
empty = set()          # {} dict hai, set nahi
unique = set([1, 2, 2, 3])
from_keys = set('banana')

a | b      # union
a & b      # intersection
a - b      # difference
a ^ b      # symmetric difference
a <= b     # subset

tags.add('ai')
tags.discard('sql')   # missing par error nahi
tags.remove('ml')     # missing par KeyError
frozen = frozenset(tags)

explain: Difference left set ke wo items deta hai jo right me nahi hain.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Sets ka basic building block hai.
Symmetric difference sirf ek side me maujood items deta hai.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.
Set difference se missing requirements aur intersection se shared skills nikalte hain.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Duplicate users/emails hatane ke liye `set(emails)` sabse sasta step hai, par order kho jata hai — report me sorted() lagao.
Permissions aur feature flags set me rakhe jate hain: do roles ka common permission intersection se milta hai.
Data reconciliation me "left me hai par right me nahi" difference se nikalta hai, aur ye list comparison se bahut fast hai.

interview.q: Set ka membership test list se fast kyun hai?
interview.a: Set hash table hai: lookup average O(1). List linear scan karti hai, isliye O(n). Bade collections me repeated `in` checks set me badal dena chahiye.

interview.q: Empty set kaise banate hain?
interview.a: `set()`. `{}` empty dict banata hai, isliye empty set ke liye constructor zaroori hai.

interview.q: Set me list kyun nahi daal sakte?
interview.a: Set ke items hashable hone chahiye, aur list unhashable/mutable hai. Tuple ya frozenset use karo.

interview.q: Duplicates hata kar original order kaise bachaye?
interview.a: `dict.fromkeys(items)` se: dict insertion order preserve karta hai, phir `list(dict.fromkeys(items))`. Set order guarantee nahi karta.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye Sets ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'
debugging.why: int() sirf poore number ka string parse karta hai. Ye Sets ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

debugging.why: String immutable hai; append list ka method hai. Ye Sets ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: String concatenation ya join use karo.
debugging.lesson: AttributeError galat type par method call ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Naam ki spelling galat hai; Python namespace me wo naam nahi milta. Ye Sets ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: NameError typo ya missing assignment batata hai.
